title: Teach the DM when to promote improvised lore
description:
Update DM runtime prompts/tool instructions to guide lore promotion.

The DM should understand when to record consequential lore and when to leave description as prose.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prompt/tool instructions define consequential lore:
  - facts that affect player choices
  - facts that create hooks
  - facts that define NPC knowledge or motives
  - facts that describe evidence/clues
  - facts that may need to be recalled later
  - consequences of player actions
- Prompt/tool instructions define decorative color:
  - sensory details
  - mood
  - incidental gestures
  - mundane props
  - non-recurring background detail
- Instructions warn against promoting every descriptive flourish.
- Instructions warn against using overlay lore to contradict module canon unless explicitly recording a consequence, reveal, or override with appropriate source/truth status.
- Examples include:
  - promote: Old Renn's mule returned alone
  - promote: axe-cuts on the north gate
  - promote: villagers may pay for investigation
  - do not promote: chipped cup
  - do not promote: damp wool smell
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.
